book.title: After Palmares: Diaspora, Inheritance, and the Afterlives of Zumbi

argument.statement: Palmares’ “afterlives” after Zumbi’s death—under an approach linking African languages, place, and diasporic spiritual beliefs—reshape how scholars can study fugitive slave communities and marronage in the African diaspora.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores the history and cultural significance of Palmares and its inhabitants within the context of the African diaspora and racial identity, making Race & Ethnicity the dominant subject.
book.summary: In After Palmares, Marc A. Hertzman tells the rise, fall, and afterlives of Palmares, one of history’s largest and longest-lasting maroon societies. Forged during the seventeenth century by formerly enslaved Africans in what would become northeast Brazil, Palmares stood for a century, withstanding sustained attacks from two European powers. In 1695, colonial forces assassinated its most famous leader, Zumbi. Hertzman examines the remarkable ways that Palmares and its inhabitants lived on after Zumbi’s death, creating vivid portraits of those whose lives and voices scholars have often assumed are inaccessible. With an innovative approach to African languages, and paying close attention to place as well as African and diasporic spiritual beliefs, Hertzman reshapes our understanding of Palmares and Zumbi and advances a new framework for studying fugitive slave communities and marronage in the African diaspora.
